headline: Low interaction risk: Botpress and Pathway have no documented shared channel, writes, or egress, so pairwise harms are mostly blocked by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress has no documented shared channel to Pathway, and Pathway exposes no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or filesystem bridge. With no direct ingestion path, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator later connects Botpress outputs into Pathway prompts or parsers, injection risk appears.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, content-based hijacking becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared prompt channels.
Disable any future copy-paste or queue-based handoff.
Add provenance tags before any cross-agent transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce input sanitization at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress and Pathway both show network_egress none, and Pathway has no filesystem read/write surfaces. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so there is no credible leakage path between them in the documented setup.
conditions: IF either agent is later given filesystem access to a shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF Botpress is configured to ingest secrets or PHI, the pair may expose them through downstream outputs.
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid placing secrets in any shared directory.
Review any future egress enablement before deployment.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls at integration points.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, but Pathway cannot execute shell, modify git state, write files, or spawn subprocesses. Without overlapping write or mutation capabilities, there is no capability conflict in the documented pair.
conditions: IF Pathway is later granted write or git mutation rights in the same directory as Botpress, conflicts can emerge.
IF an external orchestrator adds shared mutable state, concurrent writes become possible.
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only.
Do not grant Botpress shared package-management rights on production hosts.
Separate mutable resources by agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent and Pathway is a document-processing framework, but the profiles do not show Pathway acting on Botpress outputs or any downstream authority. The interaction is therefore not documented; only an inferred handoff could create cascading errors.
conditions: IF Pathway is configured to treat Botpress text as authoritative input, errors can cascade.
IF Botpress-generated content is used to trigger automated document actions, downstream mistakes become possible.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action.
Require schema validation on Botpress outputs.
Log and sample cross-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched. With no cited compliance-sensitive data flow, a compliance breach is not established for this pair.
conditions: IF EU PII or PHI is later routed through either agent, a residency or certification review is required.
IF retention policies diverge after deployment, compliance risk may appear.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Check residency requirements for any future data flow.
Set retention defaults explicitly.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and deletion controls.
